lit:
Round-1 and round-2 literature (sources opened and quoted by reviewers):
- arXiv:2605.12822 proves: r|a_i => unimodal (Cor 4.3); k=1 iff (Prop 5.3); k=2,r=2 iff (Prop 4.5).
- Unrefereed AI-assisted GitHub notes (Sept 2026): ProveIt (sufficiency b<=1+F for all r via centered peeling; necessary bound b<=1+floor(D/r); r=2 and r=3 complete criteria, the r=3 one equal to b<=1+F+2floor(t/6); 'open for k<=3 with r>=4'); AI-Has-Taste (k=2 iff for every r); omega-institute (Lean refutation of the r<=3 necessity clause via (1+q)^6(1+q^3)).
- Handelman, arXiv:1102.2961: (1+x)^m(1+x^k) is unimodal iff log-concave iff m >= k^2-3.
- Not found in any source: exact principal-value criterion; parity of the excess; closed form on the whole flat domain (only special cases known); necessity for k=3, r>=4; eventual residue determination; Conjecture S2; non-monotonicity in b; aggregate non-existence.
known:
(Notation: F = sum floor(a_i/r), D = sum(a_i-1), Gamma_t = residue-class-t sum of coefficients of A=prod[a_i]_q mod r, mu = least t in [0,r-1] with Gamma_t>=...>=Gamma_{r-1}, T6 = 1+floor((D+1-2mu)/r), U = {b: P unimodal}; a residue in [2,r-2] is 'middle'.)
- C43: r | a_i for some i => unimodal for all b.
- T1: b <= 1+F => unimodal (all r, k).
- T6 (Thm C): r divides no a_i and unimodal => b <= T6. Lemma 7: E6 = T6-1-F is always even and >= 0.
- Thm A (exact criterion): with h = two-sided (principal-value) expansion coefficients of A(q)/[r]_q and K = D+1-r(b+1): P unimodal iff h_m <= h_{K-m} for all integers 1-rb <= m < K/2. Equivalent forms: d_u = coefficients of A(q)(1-q)/(1-q^r), tau = r-periodic tail; or g = coefficients of A(q)/[r]_q: unimodal iff g_i >= g_{i-rb} for 0<=i<=floor(N/2).
- Thm E: if at most two a_i have a middle residue (always for r<=3): P unimodal iff b <= T6. (r=3: b<=1+F+2floor(S/6), S=#{a_i=2 mod 3}; r=2: b<=1+F.)
- Thm D: at most three a_i with residue outside {0,1} => unimodal iff b <= 1+F.
- Thm B (peeling): [a]_q[b]_{q^r} = [a+r(b-1)]_q + q^r[a-r]_q[b-1]_{q^r}; U(a+r e_i) contains {1} ∪ (1+U(a)). B4: if all a_i >= L0(r, residues), U = [1,F] ∪ (F + U_inf(r, residue vector)), U_inf finite, computable from 1/((1-q)^{k-1}(1-q^r)) and tau.
- T7: no function of (r,k,b,residue multiset,F,D) decides unimodality (r=6,b=4: a=(2,3,4,4,4,4,4,8) unimodal, a'=(2,2,3,4,4,4,4,10) not).
- N1: U need not be an interval (r=6, a=(2,3,3,4,4,4,5): U={1,3}).
- OPEN Conjecture S2 (from the round-1 synthesis, unproved): if r divides no a_i then U = [1,B*] or U = [1,B*] minus {B*-1}, with B* ≡ 1+F (mod 2). Equivalent: (i) b in U and b-1-F odd => b+1 in U; (ii) b in U => b' in U for all b' <= b-2.
- Literature: for r=3 and all a_i=2 the excess 2floor(t/6) is unbounded (ProveIt Cor 6.3).
box: you may compute P (or anything derived from specific parameter values) ONLY for r<=30, k<=40 (k<=60 if all a_i are equal), every a_i<=100, b anything. For instances whose coefficients exceed 2^127 use the exact big-integer checker /tmp/claude-0/qu/tools/gt_big.py (profile(r,a,bs) -> list of bools) instead of tools/uni

paths.title: Default: prove Conjecture S2 using the exact criterion (Theorem A) near the threshold.
paths.instructions: Analyse which inequalities h_m <= h_{K-m} can fail as b varies near B*, and prove (i) and (ii) of S2. Use the parity mechanism behind Lemma 7 if useful. Produce a step-by-step proof or report FAILED with the exact obstruction and numbers.

paths.title: Alternative: prove S2 by induction via peeling (Theorem B) on a_i -> a_i + r, reducing to a statement about small parts / residues.
paths.instructions: Do NOT start from the h-inequalities of Theorem A directly; build the argument on the peeling identity and the large-part limit B4, reducing S2 to a residue-level statement plus a statement about adding small parts. Prove, or report FAILED with numbers.

paths.title: Alternative: prove S2 combinatorially by a pairing / involution / injection argument on coefficient differences.
paths.instructions: Interpret coefficients of P as counts of lattice points (x_1..x_k, y) with 0<=x_i<a_i, 0<=y<b, sum x_i + r y = n. Find an explicit injection or involution showing that if b is unimodal with b-1-F odd then b+1 is unimodal, and that unimodality at b implies it at all b' <= b-2. Prove, or report FAILED with the obstruction and numbers.

paths.title: Alternative: try to REFUTE Conjecture S2 by adversarial search inside the fit box.
paths.instructions: Search structured families (all a_i equal; two values; many middle residues; composite r with many divisors such as 12, 24, 30; many a_i=1 plus a few large; a_i close to multiples of r) and use hill climbing on how close S2 comes to failing (e.g. second missing point, parity mismatch). Report any counterexample with full verification, or the closest near-misses with counts.
